origin: Own controlled finite scientific measurement-design audit. Three candidate mechanisms H1,H2,H3 describe different instrument-response hypotheses; they are not organism or clinical classes. Three settings A,B,C can provide a binary optical readout but may irreversibly lose a fragile specimen first. Calibration probabilities are exact model inputs for this audit, not uncertain estimates from experimental count data. No real instrument setting, empirical photobleaching law or deployment guarantee is asserted.
calibration_hand_off: Use every calibration row with its actual mechanism/setting identity. Deliver two reusable ordinary least-squares models with intercept: one for the positive-readout probability conditional on survival and one for loss probability. The required categorical feature order is[is_H2,is_H3,is_B,is_C,is_H2_and_B,is_H2_and_C,is_H3_and_B,is_H3_and_C], with H1/settingA as baseline. Fit all nine source rows without ridge penalty, feature scaling, target clipping, selection or train/test interpretation. Retain the exported artifacts and actual catalog predictions at all nine allowed mechanism/setting cells in row-major order H1,H2,H3 by A,B,C. Audit prediction errors against the source <=1e-9. The measurement kernel uses those actual predictions rounded to six decimal places as its explicit exact public hand-off, removing arithmetic fitting roundoff; this is not a probability-calibration or extrapolation claim. No unlisted mechanism/setting is allowed.

prior_and_limits.loss: Terminal0/1 mechanism classification error, averaged under the declared prior. There is no separate monetary or measurement-count penalty. The three loss-probability constraints are conditional on the TRUE mechanism individually, even though classification error uses a prior average.

observation_law: For hidden fixed mechanism h and attempted setting a, sample loss occurs first with probability d(h,a); it is observed, emits no binary readout and ends all measurement immediately. If the specimen survives, emit Y=1 with probability p(h,a) and Y=0 otherwise. Thus probabilities of observed outcomes LOSS,0,1 are d,(1-d)*(1-p),(1-d)*p. Conditional on h and the chosen settings, successive loss/readout randomizations are independent and the prescribed calibration does not drift. Loss is irreversible: the probability of ever losing the specimen is a first-loss probability, not an unweighted sum of per-attempt d values. A terminal mechanism decision is required even after loss. Both survival and loss can carry mechanism information.
policy_class: At the start either STOP and classify immediately, or choose A,B,C. After a surviving first readout, choose STOP or one second setting, possibly repeating the first setting. A first-attempt loss terminates; after any second-attempt outcome terminate. At every terminal history, including loss histories, choose a Bayes-optimal mechanism using the FULL likelihood of the actually observed outcomes and the declared prior. The action rule itself does not supply hidden-mechanism evidence. For a concrete tied posterior choose the lowest mechanism index; all equal-risk terminal choices are scientifically equivalent. A pure experiment strategy is STOP or the triple(first_setting,second_after_Y0,second_after_Y1). There are49 possible pure experiment strategies. Randomization may draw a pure strategy with data-independent probabilities before observing the specimen; retain the realized strategy as known design information. Equivalently, history-dependent randomized action policies with perfect recall are allowed. Neither sampling randomization nor the chosen strategy observes the true mechanism.
complete_audit: Retain all possible terminal histories of every pure strategy with their mechanism-conditional probabilities. Verify normalization, Bayes classification loss, conditional first-loss probabilities and expected attempted measurement counts. Build a complete optimization over randomized strategies, with one normalization equality and the three separate mechanism-risk limits. Retain actual catalog linear-optimization observations with valid primal and dual optimality certificates, or an equivalent complete adaptive dynamic-programming certificate accompanied by its matching optimization bound. A Monte Carlo frequency, a greedy next-test heuristic or a selected subset of promising strategies is not a complete global certificate.
comparisons: Solve the full adaptive randomized problem. Compare with the best feasible PURE strategy and with randomized OPEN-LOOP strategies, where the second action is fixed independently of the first binary readout (second_after_Y0=second_after_Y1); loss still stops measurements. Also solve the relaxation imposing ONLY prior-AVERAGED specimen-loss probability<=0.08. Report its actual conditional risks and whether it satisfies every original mechanism limit. These are different scientific constraints, not alternate numerical tolerances.
optimal_face_questions: Do not infer a unique experimental policy merely because one solver returns one optimizer. Over the ENTIRE optimal face of the original adaptive robust problem, identify the minimum and maximum probabilities of each first action STOP,A,B,C; identify the interval of prior-expected attempted measurement count; and assess the effect of a specified incorrect terminal decoder. That incorrect decoder discards all loss/survival likelihood factors, using only the positive/negative readout probabilities from successful attempts. At a loss history it conditions only on readouts obtained before the loss; after first-attempt loss it uses the original prior. Classify by that incorrect posterior with the same lowest-index tie convention. Keep the true outcome law and the already optimal experiment strategy mixture fixed. Return the minimum and maximum ACTUAL error of this wrong decoder over all optimal strategy mixtures, not an error under the wrong assumed law or a newly reoptimized experiment. All extremal intervals need global certificates; a returned witness alone does not establish identifiability.

interpretation_proposals.A: Observing specimen loss or survival can itself change mechanism probabilities when loss hazards depend on the mechanism.
interpretation_proposals.B: A prior-average risk limit automatically implies the same risk limit under each candidate mechanism.
interpretation_proposals.C: A mixed experimental strategy can outperform every feasible pure strategy under separate mechanism-risk constraints.
interpretation_proposals.D: Choosing a measurement based on the previous readout is equivalent to precommitting that measurement before the readout.
interpretation_proposals.E: Every terminal-history probability must retain both prior survival and the event that ended measurement.
interpretation_proposals.F: The loss probability of a two-attempt design is always d_first+d_second, regardless of survival and branching.
interpretation_proposals.G: Ranges over the whole optimal face distinguish an identified policy property from an arbitrary optimizer witness.
interpretation_proposals.H: Exact saturated calibration models establish probability accuracy at unobserved conditions or a validated real specimen-loss law.

reporting: pure_strategy_count; openloop_pure_strategy_count; best_feasible_pure_error; best_feasible_pure_strategy_ids; optimal_adaptive_robust_error; optimal_openloop_robust_error; optimal_average_risk_only_error; average_risk_relaxation_conditional_loss_probabilities inH1,H2,H3 order; average_risk_relaxation_meets_all_model_limits asboolean; optimal_first_action_probability_intervals mapsSTOP,A,B,C to[min,max]; optimal_expected_attempted_measurement_interval; optimal_face_error_if_loss_information_ignored_interval; randomization_strictly_improves_over_pure and adaptivity_strictly_improves_over_openloop asbooleans; valid_interpretation_proposal_ids. Strategy IDs are STOP orstart:A|0:S|1:B etc, withS denoting stop; construct all first-setting/second-action combinations in the stated semantics. Counts, IDs, booleans exact; numeric absolute tolerance1e-8. Full calibrated-model artifacts, actual predictions, all branch laws, primal/dual and optimal-face certificates belong in the trajectory.

methodological_source.title: Bayesian Experimental Design: A Review
methodological_source.role: Decision-theoretic context for experimental design with explicit expected utility. The finite response panel, irreversible-loss risks and constrained adaptive problem here are own constructions, not data or a claimed result from that review.
